name: Bradley Mottier Innovation Challenge in Systems Engineering
tagline: Fall business-plan competition for engineering teams with ISE students
description: A fall competition from Illinois ISE where teams of 2 to 4 Grainger students (at least 2 in ISE) develop an innovation into a business plan, submit reports, and present in December for prizes of $5,000, $2,000, and $1,000.
what_it_is: A September to December competition run by the Industrial and Enterprise Systems Engineering (ISE) department in which small teams develop an innovation idea into a business plan, turn in reports, and present to judges for cash prizes.
who_should_apply: Grainger Engineering undergrad or grad teams of 2 to 4 with at least 2 ISE students and an idea they want to develop into a business plan.
choose_this_if: You are an ISE student who wants a structured fall semester to turn an idea into a judged business plan with prize money on the line.
good_for: ISE students developing an innovation with prize money
parent_org: Department of Industrial and Enterprise Systems Engineering (ISE)
ideal_participant: Grainger Engineering teams of 2 to 4 with at least 2 ISE students
apply_steps: Form a team of 2 to 4 Grainger students with at least 2 ISE members | Submit the online application for committee approval by the September deadline | Turn in midterm and final reports, then give a final presentation
deadline_note: 2026 applications closed Sept 13, 2026 (kickoff Sept 17). Accepted 2026 teams still have final reports due Nov 29, the final presentation Dec 4, and winners announced Dec 10, 2026. The program page says it runs September through December each year, so the 2027 application deadline should fall in early to mid September 2027; no date posted yet (source: ise.illinois.edu/mottier).
cost_or_funding: Prizes of $5,000, $2,000, and $1,000, plus up to $500 expense reimbursement per team (per program page)
notes: Status evidence: ise.illinois.edu/mottier lists the 2026 timeline with the final presentation on Dec 4, 2026 and winners on Dec 10, 2026, so the current cycle is in progress. No more than 3 graduate students per team. Contact is Julie Murphy, ISE Director of Alumni Relations. next_deadline is the 2026 final presentation, relevant only to accepted teams.

name: Cozad New Venture Challenge
tagline: Campus-wide spring startup competition with workshops, mentors, and big prizes
description: UIUC's largest startup competition, run by the Landuyt Center each spring. Students register an idea, get track-based workshops and mentors, pitch at Demo Day, and compete for prizes that topped $700,000 in 2026, including a $100,000 grand prize.
what_it_is: The Landuyt Center's yearly spring program where students register an idea, attend track-based workshops with mentors, pitch at a Demo Day, and compete at finals for cash prizes and SAFE investments (simple agreements for future equity).
who_should_apply: Any full-time UIUC undergrad or grad student, solo or on a team, at any stage from a raw idea to a running startup; no prototype needed.
choose_this_if: You want to turn a startup idea into a pitch-ready venture over one spring semester and compete for real funding.
good_for: Turning a startup idea into a funded venture
ideal_participant: Any full-time UIUC student, solo or on a team, with a startup idea; the online track is limited to Gies iMBA and MCS Chicago students
apply_steps: Register yourself or your team before the registration deadline | Attend the kickoff, virtual orientation, and track workshops | Pitch at Demo Day to compete for a spot in the finals
deadline_note: The Cozad FAQ says 2027 registration opens in Fall 2026. The Landuyt calendar lists weekly 'Cozad Registration' entries from Dec 1, 2026 through Feb 2, 2027 but does not state a deadline. The 2026 registration deadline was Feb 1, 2026, with Demo Day Apr 16 and finals Apr 17, 2026 (schedule page). Earlier step: SocialFuse, a team-building and pitching night with Cozad Q&A, is Nov 5, 2026, 5 to 7 pm at the CIF Monumental Steps (Landuyt calendar).
cost_or_funding: Over $700,000 in prizes and investments awarded in 2026, including a $100,000 Grand Prize (per program page)
notes: Status evidence: Cozad FAQ states 2027 registration opens in Fall 2026, and the Landuyt calendar shows Cozad Registration entries from Dec 1, 2026 to Feb 2, 2027 plus a Nov 5, 2026 SocialFuse event. Online track is limited to Gies iMBA and MCS Chicago students. Schedule page still shows the 2026 timeline.

name: Health Make-A-Thon
tagline: Carle Illinois health-care prototyping contest that feeds into Cozad
description: A Carle Illinois Health Maker Lab competition where medical-student-led teams prototype fixes for patient problems and pitch to judges. The 2025 edition was a two-day patient-centered event with a $10,000 prize pool, and it serves as a path into Cozad's health care track.
what_it_is: A short design-and-pitch competition from the Carle Illinois College of Medicine's Health Maker Lab where teams led by medical students build prototypes for real patient problems and pitch them to judges for prize money.
who_should_apply: Mainly Carle Illinois medical students; students from design, engineering, business, and liberal arts have joined medical-student-led teams, but entry rules for a 2026 edition are not posted.
choose_this_if: You are a medical student, or want to team up with one, and want to prototype a health-care product in a short, judged sprint.
good_for: Prototyping a health solution in a short team competition
parent_org: Health Maker Lab, Carle Illinois College of Medicine
ideal_participant: Carle Illinois medical students and collaborators from design, engineering, and business
apply_steps: Sign up for competition updates through the form on the Health Maker Lab events page
deadline_note: The Health Maker Lab events page calls it a Fall Make-a-Thon. The latest edition was a two-day patient-centered event in fall 2025 (Carle Illinois news story dated Dec 11, 2025). No fall 2026 date appears on the events page or the Carle Illinois events calendar as of 2026-10-13.
cost_or_funding: 2025 edition had a $10,000 prize pool ($5,000, $3,000, $2,000 for top three) per the Dec 2025 Carle Illinois news story; 2026 prizes not posted.
notes: Status evidence: Events page describes a recurring fall competition but lists no 2026 date; the most recent news is the Dec 11, 2025 story on the 2025 edition, and the Carle Illinois calendar shows no Make-a-Thon in late 2026. Format has changed over time. Early editions (2018 to 2020) were open to all Illinois residents with $10,000 in lab resources for each of 10 winners. The current events page describes a Fall Make-a-Thon for CI MED students that feeds into the Cozad New Venture Challenge health care track. 2025 teams included students from Art and Design, Gies, Grainger, and LAS. Updates sign-up form: https://forms.illinois.edu/sec/549661001.

name: EnterpriseWorks Incubator (and EW 2.0)
tagline: Research Park startup incubator with labs, offices, and expert advising
description: Research Park's startup incubator, offering wet labs, offices, entrepreneur-in-residence advising, SBIR grant help, and events to early-stage tech companies from the university and community. Tenants must be incorporated for-profit companies. A growth-stage EW 2.0 building is planned.
what_it_is: The University of Illinois Research Park's incubator, which rents wet labs and offices to early-stage tech companies and connects them with entrepreneurs-in-residence, SBIR grant help, and events; a growth-stage building called EW 2.0 is planned next door.
who_should_apply: Incorporated, early-stage tech companies with university or community founders; student founders use a separate student startup membership instead (see the EnterpriseWorks shared space entry).
choose_this_if: You are running an incorporated tech startup that needs lab or office space and hands-on advising near campus.
good_for: Getting lab or office space and incubation for a tech startup
parent_org: Research Park / Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation
ideal_participant: University and community founders with a tech venture who need space and incubation
apply_steps: Check the tenant criteria on the Becoming a Tenant page | Submit the online EnterpriseWorks tenant application | Contact Cynthia Faullin (cfaullin@illinois.edu) to discuss space options
deadline_note: No deadline posted. An Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article says the incubator takes companies on a continuous basis but is currently fully leased.
cost_or_funding: Rent and fees not published; contact EnterpriseWorks staff for pricing
notes: Status evidence: Incubator page shows news through Aug 21, 2026, and an Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article describes current EnterpriseWorks programs and the planned EW 2.0 building. EW 2.0 = 'EnterpriseWorks 2.0', a planned growth-stage incubator building adjacent to EnterpriseWorks, funded by state capital including a DCEO Tech Incubator Enhancement Grant and IFAB Tech Hub funding; as of Aug 21, 2026 still described as plans, no opening date. The /enterpriseworks footer link redirects to an unrelated news article (EnterpriseWorks awarded University Center grant), so use the locate-here page. Contact email is the general Research Park address.

name: EnterpriseWorks Incubator (labs, offices, and makerspace)
tagline: Shared lab, coworking, and makerspace access for startups at EnterpriseWorks
description: Shared coworking, wet lab, and makerspace space at Research Park's EnterpriseWorks incubator. Students with a for-profit tech startup can apply for a student startup membership, awarded competitively, with most spots going to Cozad and Illinois Innovation Award winners.
what_it_is: Shared coworking, wet lab, and makerspace space at the EnterpriseWorks incubator, with tools such as 3D printers, laser cutters, a lathe, and a mill, open to tenants, affiliate members, and selected student startups.
who_should_apply: Student founders of a for-profit tech startup with a currently enrolled Illinois founder or executive; most student space goes to Cozad and Illinois Innovation Award winners.
choose_this_if: You are a student founder who needs shared lab or coworking space and your startup already has traction, such as a Cozad award.
good_for: Finding lab, office, and prototyping space for a tech startup
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: Student founders of a for-profit tech startup, especially Cozad or Illinois Innovation Award winners, plus tenants and affiliate members needing shared lab or shop space
apply_steps: Confirm a founder or executive is a current Illinois student and the startup is a for-profit tech business | Submit the EnterpriseWorks student startup application | Expect a competitive review, since shared space is not guaranteed
deadline_note: No deadline listed on the Becoming a Tenant page; student proposals are reviewed competitively. An Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article says EnterpriseWorks takes companies on a continuous basis.
cost_or_funding: Makerspace described as free for Research Park companies, EnterpriseWorks tenants, and affiliate members (2019 page); student membership cost not published
notes: Status evidence: Becoming a Tenant page links a live student startup application; Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article lists Student Shared Services among current EnterpriseWorks programs. Makerspace page (dated 2019) says it is free for Research Park companies, EnterpriseWorks tenants, and affiliate members; individual students without a resident company are not listed as eligible. Rent and tenancy criteria are not published.

name: I-Start Program
tagline: Former 2011 pilot that subsidized first-year services for university spinouts
description: A 2011 EnterpriseWorks pilot, funded by an Illinois state grant, that covered part of the cost of first-year services like legal setup, business plans, and SBIR applications for about 15 university spinouts. No sign it still runs; Catapult now covers similar services.
what_it_is: A pilot program announced by EnterpriseWorks in July 2011 that shared the cost of first-year business services such as business plans, legal setup, SBIR grant applications, accounting, and HR for new University of Illinois startups.
who_should_apply: Not open to students; it targeted University of Illinois faculty inventors and other founders in 2011, and no current version of the program was found.
choose_this_if: You are researching past startup support at Research Park; for help paying for early services today, look at the Catapult program instead.
good_for: New university spinouts needing first-year business services
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: University of Illinois faculty or other entrepreneurs launching a company around a university technology
deadline_note: Only source is a July 25, 2011 announcement describing an 18-month pilot for about 15 startups. No later application cycle found.
notes: Status evidence: The 2011 article is the only official mention; the Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article lists current EnterpriseWorks programs (EIR, SBIR help, Student Shared Services, Catapult) and does not include I-Start. Likely defunct: the only official source is a July 2011 announcement of a state-funded (DCEO) pilot covering about 15 startups over 18 months. It is not named among current EnterpriseWorks programs in the Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article. The Catapult program now offers similar subsidized services. Recommend removing or marking inactive unless EnterpriseWorks confirms it still runs.

name: iVenture Accelerator
tagline: Paid 10-week summer accelerator for student startups at Gies
description: Gies College of Business's 10-week, full-time summer accelerator for student startups. Teams get up to $20,000 in non-dilutive funding and stipends with no equity taken, plus mentors, workshops, and investor connections. Applications are reviewed in waves from fall to March.
what_it_is: A full-time, 10-week summer accelerator run by the Gies College of Business where student startup teams get up to $20,000 in non-dilutive funding (no equity taken), mentors, workshops, and ties to Chicago startup hubs, followed by programming through the school year.
who_should_apply: University of Illinois student founders with up to 4 teammates who are already working on a venture and can commit full-time for 10 weeks in summer; preference goes to teams not graduating that summer.
choose_this_if: You want to work on your startup full-time over the summer with funding and stipends instead of taking an internship.
good_for: Student founders ready to work full-time on a startup over the summer
parent_org: Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, Gies College of Business
ideal_participant: A University of Illinois student founder with up to 4 teammates (majority Illinois students holding majority ownership) who can commit 10 weeks full-time in summer
apply_steps: Have one team member submit the online application covering your venture, team, progress, and references | Answer any follow-up questions from program staff | Interview with the committee if your team is chosen as a finalist
deadline_note: Summer 2026 cohort: Wave 1 closed Nov 3, 2025 and the final wave closed March 7, 2026, with rolling feedback between waves (apply page). The apply page has not been updated for summer 2027 as of 2026-10-13. If the pattern holds, Wave 1 for summer 2027 would close in early November 2026, so contact iventure@illinois.edu now for the date or an early review.
cost_or_funding: Up to $20,000 non-dilutive ($10,000 capacity funding plus $2,500 stipends for up to 4 full-time team members); no equity taken (per iventure.illinois.edu). Non-Illinois team members do not receive stipends.
notes: Status evidence: Gies news dated June 24, 2026 announces iVenture's 12th cohort (15 teams) for summer 2026, followed by 11 months of programming through the academic year. Run by the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship at Gies (formerly OVAEL). A June 2026 Gies story says the program now serves students across the University of Illinois System, including UIC, and incubated at TechNexus in Chicago in summer 2025 and 2026. The cohort continues with 11 months of programming during the school year. Related credit courses: BADM 463/464 iVenture Accelerator Seminars.

name: AWARE (Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship)
tagline: Landuyt program of starter courses, mentoring, and small prizes for new founders
description: A Landuyt Center program that eases students of any major into entrepreneurship with intro courses, advising, mentor office hours, Maker Money grants of up to $500, and AWARE Prizes that fund early-stage teams in the Cozad New Venture Challenge.
what_it_is: A Landuyt Center umbrella program that helps students new to entrepreneurship through intro courses (TE 198 FIE, TE 401 AWR), advising, mentor office hours, Maker Money grants of up to $500, and AWARE Prizes for early-stage Cozad teams.
who_should_apply: Any UIUC student of any major or background who is curious about entrepreneurship or has an early idea; no experience needed.
choose_this_if: You are new to entrepreneurship and want a low-pressure way in through a course, a mentor, or a small grant before or during Cozad.
good_for: First-time founders who want a course, a mentor, or a small grant to get started
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student, any major or background, curious about entrepreneurship or holding an early idea
apply_steps: Enroll in TE 198 FIE to build basic entrepreneurship skills | Take TE 401 AWR to develop your own project for the Cozad New Venture Challenge | Join Cozad as an early-stage team to be considered for AWARE Prizes
deadline_note: No AWARE-specific deadline posted. AWARE Prizes go to early-stage Cozad teams, so Cozad registration (2026 deadline was Feb 1, 2026; 2027 registration opens Fall 2026) is the likely gate, but the page does not say how prize winners are picked.
cost_or_funding: Free courses and advising; Maker Money grants up to $500; AWARE Prize amounts not posted
notes: Status evidence: The current Landuyt site (2026) lists AWARE under Programs with live links to courses, advising, Maker Money, mentor office hours, and AWARE Prizes. The older EnterpriseWorks AWARE page (researchpark.illinois.edu/AWARE) returns 404. AWARE now lives at the Landuyt Center (landuyt.illinois.edu/programs/aware) as an umbrella for TE 198 FIE, TE 401 AWR, Entrepreneurship Advising, Maker Money, Office Hours with Mentors, and AWARE Prizes for Cozad teams. Faculty lead: Keilin Jahnke. Earlier, AWARE (Accelerating Women and underRepresented Entrepreneurs) was an NSF-funded EnterpriseWorks program (award #1464507, 2015 to 2019); a 2021 Gies story reported a Cozad AWARE award. The current page no longer spells out the acronym and frames the program as open to everyone. Old page researchpark.illinois.edu/AWARE returns 404. Overlaps with any separate Maker Money or Office Hours entries.

name: Catherine and Don Kleinmuntz Center for Genomics in Business and Society
tagline: IGB genomics center that funded faculty proof-of-concept and grad innovation training
description: A donor-funded center at IGB that has offered $50,000 to $75,000 proof-of-concept grants to IGB faculty and a 10-week summer innovation course with $5,000 to $20,000 awards for IGB grad students and postdocs. No new cycle has been posted since 2023.
what_it_is: A donor-funded center at the Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology (IGB) that has funded proof-of-concept grants for IGB faculty (Mikashi Awards) and a 10-week summer innovation course with prizes for IGB grad students and postdocs (Young Innovator Program).
who_should_apply: Not open to most students; IGB faculty apply for Mikashi Awards, and IGB grad students and postdocs with their PI's approval could apply to the Young Innovator Program.
choose_this_if: You are an IGB grad student or postdoc who wants training and seed money to take genomics research toward real-world use.
good_for: Proof-of-concept funding for IGB genomics research
parent_org: Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology (IGB)
ideal_participant: IGB faculty (Mikashi Awards); IGB grad students and postdocs (Young Innovator Program, PSCB seminars)
deadline_note: Last Young Innovator Program call found was for summer 2023, with applications due April 24, 2023 and the course running May 30 to Aug 8, 2023 (IGB program page). The center's own news page stops in Aug 2022. No 2026 or 2027 cycle found.
cost_or_funding: Mikashi Awards: up to two awards per year of $50,000 to $75,000 for up to two years; Young Innovator Program: tiered awards of $5,000 to $20,000 to three cohort members (per https://kleinmuntzcenter.illinois.edu/programs; currency of these amounts unverified)
notes: Status evidence: kleinmuntzcenter.illinois.edu news ends Aug 24, 2022; the IGB Young Innovator page still shows the 2023 cycle; no 2025 or 2026 activity found. Map lists it as 'Kleinmuntz Center' under IGB; full name is the Catherine and Don Kleinmuntz Center for Genomics in Business and Society. News stops in 2022; the Young Innovator Program may have been folded into or superseded by the IGB Early Innovator Program (similar 10-week summer format), but no page confirms this. Possibly dormant.

name: EnterpriseWorks Catapult New Venture Program
tagline: Subsidy covering 80% of early legal, accounting, and grant-writing costs for spinouts
description: An EnterpriseWorks award that pays 80% of early professional services, up to $5,000 for one year, such as legal setup, bookkeeping, SBIR applications, and branding, for pre-formation startups using UIUC-licensed technology. Winners must become EnterpriseWorks tenants.
what_it_is: An EnterpriseWorks award that pays 80% of the cost, up to $5,000 over one year, of early professional services such as legal setup, bookkeeping, SBIR grant applications, and branding for a startup forming around University of Illinois technology.
who_should_apply: Founders, including student teams, of a not-yet-formed startup whose technology is licensed or being licensed from UIUC and who are willing to become EnterpriseWorks tenants.
choose_this_if: You want to cut the cost of lawyers, accountants, and grant writers while forming a company around a UIUC-licensed technology.
good_for: Covering legal and setup costs when forming a university-linked startup
ideal_participant: Pre-formation University of Illinois affiliated founders, including Cozad student teams, with technology licensed or being licensed from UIUC
apply_steps: Confirm your company is pre-formation and its technology is licensed or being licensed from UIUC | Submit the online Catapult application | If selected, become an EnterpriseWorks tenant to use the award
deadline_note: Program page says applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline. Student teams have also received Catapult Awards as Cozad New Venture Challenge prizes (2025).
cost_or_funding: EnterpriseWorks covers 80% of service costs up to $5,000 for one year (per program page); awardees must become EnterpriseWorks tenants
notes: Status evidence: Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article names the Catapult New Venture Program among current EnterpriseWorks programs; program page (dated Jan 29, 2021) still links a live application form. Program page is dated January 29, 2021, so terms may be outdated, but the program is named in 2025 and 2026 Research Park news. Not on the map's EnterpriseWorks or Research Park lists. The related Student Startup Tenancy award is likely covered by the map's 'Incubator labs, offices, & maker space' entry.

name: Illinois Innovation Award
tagline: $20,000 nominated award for a UIUC student's high-impact innovation or research
description: Grainger Engineering's yearly $20,000 award, run by the Landuyt Center, for a UIUC student whose innovation or translational research could have major impact. Students cannot apply directly; a faculty member, mentor, or campus unit submits a nomination.
what_it_is: A yearly Grainger Engineering award, run by the Landuyt Center, that gives one UIUC student $20,000 and a trophy for an innovation or translational research project (research moved toward real-world use) with major potential impact.
who_should_apply: Full-time, on-campus UIUC undergrad or grad students who are the main inventor, founder, or researcher on their work; a faculty member, mentor, or campus unit must nominate you, since students cannot nominate themselves.
choose_this_if: You are a student whose innovation or research has real-world impact and you have a mentor or advisor willing to nominate you.
good_for: Recognition and cash for a high-impact student innovation
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship (Grainger College of Engineering)
ideal_participant: Full-time on-campus UIUC students with an impactful innovation or research translation, nominated by a mentor or unit
apply_steps: Ask a faculty member, mentor, advisor, or campus unit to nominate you | Give your nominator a letter describing your role in the work plus your resume | Have your nominator submit the nomination form with their letter by the deadline
deadline_note: Program page says nominations for the 2026-27 cycle open in Fall 2026 and the winner is named at a Spring 2027 ceremony; no deadline or form link posted yet as of 2026-10-13. Past nomination deadline: Jan 22, 2024 (Landuyt calendar). 2026 recipients were announced Apr 30, 2026, after an Apr 17, 2026 ceremony.
cost_or_funding: $20,000 award plus trophy (per program page)
notes: Status evidence: landuyt.illinois.edu/programs/iip describes eligibility for the 2026-2027 academic year with applications opening Fall 2026; Landuyt news dated Apr 30, 2026 names the 2026 recipients. Page is titled Illinois Innovation Award & Fiddler Innovation Fellowship. The Fiddler Innovation Fellowship ($10,000, awarded by the eDream Institute at NCSA) honors interdisciplinary innovation that mixes creativity, art or design, and technology; the same student cannot be nominated for both. Each unit may submit at most two nominations. Winners are expected to help promote the program the following year.

name: Illinois Proof-of-Concept Program (IPOC)
tagline: Up to $50,000 grant for faculty to prove a campus invention is market-ready
description: An Office of Technology Management grant of up to $50,000 that helps Illinois faculty turn a disclosed invention into a prototype or proven product. Students cannot apply as the lead, but awards can pay grad and undergrad students working on the project.
what_it_is: A yearly Office of Technology Management grant of up to $50,000, paid in stages, that funds faculty-led projects such as prototypes or feasibility tests to move a disclosed University of Illinois invention toward licensing or a startup.
who_should_apply: Not open to students as applicants; full-time Illinois academic researchers with an invention report on file apply, and grad or undergrad students can be paid to work on funded projects.
choose_this_if: You are a student in a lab with a promising invention and want your PI to seek funding that could pay you to build it out.
good_for: Funding faculty-led work to prove an invention is commercially viable
ideal_participant: Full-time Illinois academic researchers (or emeritus faculty with active labs) with an invention report on file at OTM; students can be paid on projects
apply_steps: File an invention disclosure with OTM if one is not already on file | Fill in the IPOC slide-deck application template | Submit the application online; finalists then pitch to an external committee
deadline_note: The 2026 program guide (dated Dec 2, 2025) set a Feb 27, 2026 deadline, with awards announced May 2026 for projects starting summer 2026. The 2026 window is closed and 2027 dates are not posted; last cycle the guide appeared in early December with a late February deadline.
cost_or_funding: Up to $50,000 per project, paid in tranches (per OTM IPOC page)
notes: Status evidence: OTM IPOC page says 2026 awards were announced May 2026 for projects starting summer 2026, so funded projects are running now; the 2026 application window is marked closed. Students cannot apply as PI but can be paid from awards. OTM selects up to 6 awardees per cycle. IP from funded work is owned by the University. Funds cannot go to a startup company or pay PI salaries. General OTM email: otm@illinois.edu.

name: Illinois Ventures
tagline: University of Illinois System venture fund investing in startups with Illinois ties
description: The University of Illinois System's venture capital arm. It invests equity at pre-seed, seed, and Series A stages in deep tech and other high-growth startups with Illinois ties, and runs an alumni angel network. Founders pitch through an online form.
what_it_is: The University of Illinois System's venture capital arm, which makes pre-seed, seed, and Series A equity investments in deep tech and other high-growth startups with a University of Illinois connection, and runs an alumni angel network (Illini Angels).
who_should_apply: Founders of a startup with a University of Illinois tie, from student dorm-room teams to faculty spinouts, who are raising a pre-seed to Series A round.
choose_this_if: You are raising an equity round for a high-growth startup with University of Illinois roots and want a university-affiliated investor.
good_for: Raising seed or pre-seed equity for a university-connected tech startup
ideal_participant: Founders of high-growth tech startups with a University of Illinois connection, including student and faculty teams
apply_steps: Fill out the Becoming a Portfolio Company form with your company, university affiliation, and round stage | Attach your pitch deck | Or email pitch@illinoisventures.com directly
deadline_note: Pitches accepted anytime through the online form or by email; no deadline.
notes: Status evidence: illinoisventures.com (copyright 2026) has a live pitch form on its Becoming a Portfolio Company page; latest news post is July 21, 2025, and it launched a new deep tech fund in Oct 2024. Offices in Champaign (60 Hazelwood Drive) and Chicago. Pitch email: pitch@illinoisventures.com. Investment sizes are not published. Programs: Deep Tech Fund (seed and Series A), Pre-Seed Fund, and Illini Angels alumni network. The map lists an Illinois Ventures Evergreen Fund; no official Illinois Ventures page mentions it, so it is merged here until someone confirms it exists.

name: Brand Hub Professional Online Certificates and Development
tagline: Online branding and advertising training from a College of Media hub (unverified)
description: Branding and advertising certificates listed on the campus ecosystem map under the College of Media's Brand Hub. No current official page describes them, so check with the Advertising department before planning around this.
what_it_is: Online professional certificates in branding and advertising that the ecosystem map credits to the Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology, a College of Media center whose website could not be reached.
who_should_apply: Unclear; no current page confirms who can enroll or whether the certificates still exist.
choose_this_if: You want to build branding and advertising skills and are willing to confirm the offering with the College of Media first.
good_for: Learning branding and advertising skills online
parent_org: Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology (Brand Hub)
ideal_participant: Students and professionals wanting branding and advertising training
deadline_note: No dates found. The Brand Hub site did not respond on 2026-10-13.
notes: Status evidence: brandhub.illinois.edu returned no content when fetched on 2026-10-13. A web search found only 2021 to 2022 news about Brand Hub programs, such as a summer academy with a certificate and an Amazon Ads course, but no current certificate page. Brand Hub site unreachable (DNS failure on 2026-10-13); no certificate page found. The College of Media separately offers online graduate certificates in Strategic Brand Communication and an online MS in Strategic Brand Communication (listed at online.illinois.edu), which may be what this entry refers to or its successor; these are paid academic programs, not Brand Hub branded. Consider merging into brand-hub or dropping.

name: Design Thinking Courses (DTX)
tagline: For-credit design thinking and UX courses open to students in any major
description: Siebel Center for Design teaches DTX courses on design thinking, human-centered design, UX tools, and design ethics, open to any major. Students learn user interviews, journey maps, wireframes, and prototyping through team projects; DTX 180 also counts for a Gen Ed.
what_it_is: A set of credit courses with the DTX code, taught by the Siebel Center for Design, that teach human-centered design, user research, prototyping, and UX tools through team projects.
who_should_apply: Undergraduates from any major, with no design or programming background needed for the intro courses.
choose_this_if: You want to learn how to interview users, map their needs, and prototype a product idea for course credit.
good_for: Learning human-centered design and user research for credit
ideal_participant: Undergraduates from any major wanting design thinking, UX, and innovation skills
deadline_note: No program deadline; enroll during normal campus course registration. Courses page lists Fall 2026 offerings.
notes: Status evidence: The Courses page lists Fall 2026 DTX courses, including DTX 180, 221, 251, and several DTX 495 special topics (Student Centered App Design, Ethics in HCD, Intro to UX Theory and Tools, Designing with Data). description: A Gies College of Business 3D printing lab where students print parts for a $4 base fee plus 10 cents per gram, order prints online, or pay staff designers $20 per hour to model a prototype.
what_it_is: A 3D printing lab in the Gies Business Instructional Facility where students can print parts at a walk-in counter or order online, hire staff designers to model a prototype, and take 3D design workshops and courses.
who_should_apply: Any UIUC student, faculty, or staff member who needs a 3D printed part or design help; the public can also use it at higher rates.
choose_this_if: You want a cheap 3D printed prototype fast, or want to pay a staff designer to turn your idea into a 3D model.
good_for: Quick 3D printed prototypes and learning digital fabrication
ideal_participant: UIUC students and faculty who need to 3D print a prototype or learn 3D design
apply_steps: Visit Room 3030 of the Business Instructional Facility during lab hours to print at the walk-in rate | Or place an order through the online ordering page | Use the contact form to request design help or tutoring
deadline_note: Fall 2026 hours effective August 31, 2026: Monday and Friday 1 to 7 PM, Tuesday and Thursday 2 to 7 PM, Wednesday 4 to 7 PM (lab hours page). Closed on university holidays, Spring Break, and Thanksgiving week. Summer 2027 camp dates to be posted in early 2027.
cost_or_funding: Students: $4 base fee per print plus 10 cents per gram walk-in (12 cents online); design and prototyping help $20 per hour; private 3D modeling tutoring $25 per 30 minutes
notes: Status evidence: Homepage banner says Fall 2026 is open, and the lab hours page lists Fall 2026 hours effective August 31, 2026. Room 3030, Business Instructional Facility, 515 E. Gregory Dr., Champaign. Billed as the first business school 3D printing lab. Uses Ultimaker printers; dual color or special filament adds 50 percent. Contact is through a web form (no email shown on fetched pages). Also runs youth summer camps and related courses such as BADM 331 Making Things.

name: Jackson Innovation Studio (MechSE MakerWorks)
tagline: MechSE makerspace with low-cost 3D printing and free laser cutters
description: A Mechanical Engineering makerspace open weekdays 11am to 10pm with 3D printing from 3 cents per gram and free laser cutters if you bring material. Undergrad volunteers get 24/7 access and free materials.
what_it_is: A makerspace in the Sidney Lu Mechanical Engineering Building with 3D printers, laser cutters, hand tools, and student volunteers who help you use them, open to anyone on weekdays.
who_should_apply: Any UIUC student, from any major, building a physical prototype; undergrads who volunteer with the MakerWorks Club get 24/7 access.
choose_this_if: You want the cheapest on-campus 3D printing and free laser cutting for a physical prototype.
good_for: Building low-cost physical prototypes
parent_org: Department of Mechanical Science and Engineering, Grainger College of Engineering
ideal_participant: Students building hardware prototypes; undergrads who volunteer get 24/7 access
apply_steps: Visit during open hours and ask an on-duty volunteer for training | Ask a volunteer to add you to the 3D printer queue | Bring or buy your own material for the laser cutters
deadline_note: No deadlines. Open 11am to 10pm Monday to Friday to all visitors; 24/7 for MakerWorks Club volunteers. Design class students get priority during their deadline weeks.
cost_or_funding: 3D printing filament per gram (PLA $0.03, PETG and ABS $0.04, TPU $0.05); laser cutters free, bring or buy material; card payments, $1 minimum; volunteers get up to $50 per semester free
notes: Status evidence: Studio page lists current open hours and a note about limited hours until 9/16, and links a Spring 2026 awards program; page copyright 2026. Sidney Lu Mechanical Engineering Building, 1206 W. Green St., Urbana. Mainly supports MechSE courses, but open to all students and employees. Personal filament not allowed. One printer per person at a time. Wood Maker Studio is limited to trained volunteers and MechSE design students. To volunteer (undergrads only, any major), join the MakerWorks Slack and the #new-volunteers channel. RSOs can rent the studio by email.

name: Siebel Center for Design
tagline: Campus design center with free makerspace labs, design workshops, and bookable rooms
description: A UIUC design center that teaches human-centered design and offers free-to-use maker labs (pay only for materials), a media studio, and rooms students can book at no cost for team meetings and events.
what_it_is: A campus building and program that teaches human-centered design (designing around user needs) through courses, certificates, and workshops, and houses labs for lasers, CNC, 3D printing, electronics, textiles, and media plus rooms students can book for free.
who_should_apply: Any UIUC student, faculty, or staff member; no design background needed.
choose_this_if: You want to learn how to design a product around real users and have a free place to prototype and meet as a team.
good_for: Learning design thinking and prototyping a product
ideal_participant: Students of any major who want design skills or a place to build prototypes
apply_steps: Complete the general online orientation in Canvas before using any lab | Book meeting or event rooms through the online reservation portal at least 48 hours ahead | Register for HCD or Maker Workshops on the workshops page
deadline_note: No program deadline. Spring 2027 room reservations open November 1 (FAQ). Upcoming registration-required Maker Workshops include October 19, October 26, and November 2, 2026 (workshops page).
cost_or_funding: Free for students to use equipment and book rooms; pay only for materials used
notes: Status evidence: Workshops page lists upcoming events in October and November 2026, and lab hours are posted for the current fall semester. 1208 S. Fourth St., Champaign. Labs open Tuesday to Friday 4 to 10 PM and weekends 1 to 6 PM during fall and spring; closed in summer. Media Studio booked through Skedda after a Canvas orientation. Many programs (SHIFT) target K-12 educators rather than founders. See The Shop entry for makerspace details.

name: The Shop (Siebel Center for Design)
tagline: Siebel Center makerspace with free tool use after online orientation and training
description: The Siebel Center for Design makerspace with laser, CNC, 3D printing, wood, electronics, and textile labs. After an online orientation and staff training, students use the tools free and pay only for materials.
what_it_is: The makerspace on the lower level of the Siebel Center for Design with 3D printing, laser, CNC, woodworking, electronics, textiles, and print labs, where staff train you on a tool before you use it on your own.
who_should_apply: UIUC students, faculty, and staff at any skill level, including complete beginners.
choose_this_if: You want to learn to use lasers, CNC, or wood tools yourself and build a prototype paying only for materials.
good_for: Building physical prototypes with shop tools
ideal_participant: Students building hardware or physical prototypes who want access to fabrication tools and training
apply_steps: Complete the general and lab-specific online orientations in Canvas | Come on a Training Day and check in at The Shop front desk for in-person tool training | Return on Production Days to build on your own
deadline_note: No deadline. Training Days are Tuesday and Friday 4 to 10 PM and Saturday 1 to 6 PM; Production Days are Wednesday and Thursday 4 to 10 PM and Sunday 1 to 6 PM. Monday is reserved for registered Maker Workshops (next: October 19, October 26, November 2, 2026). Labs close the Friday after Reading Day and all summer.
cost_or_funding: Free equipment use; pay only for materials (basic materials sold on site, or bring your own after staff approval). Maker Workshops include supplies
notes: Status evidence: Maker Workshops page lists sessions at The Shop on October 19, October 26, November 2, and November 9, 2026, and The Shop page shows the current weekly schedule. Lower level of the Siebel Center for Design, 1208 S. Fourth St., Champaign. All labs require Canvas orientation before the first visit. Maker Workshops (Mondays 4:30 to 7 PM) are beginner friendly, need registration, and require orientation. A pay-per-page laser printer is available during open hours.

name: Translational Research Facility
tagline: Unverified map entry; no UIUC facility with this exact name was found
description: A biomedical translational research space named on the UIUC ecosystem map that could not be matched to any official facility page. Treat as unverified until its identity is confirmed.
what_it_is: A name listed on the UIUC ecosystem map with no link; no official UIUC page describes a facility by this exact name.
who_should_apply: Unclear; no access process or eligibility could be found.
choose_this_if: You are a biomedical researcher trying to identify campus spaces for moving lab work toward clinical use.
good_for: Unclear; needs verification
ideal_participant: Biomedical researchers moving work toward clinical use (if the facility exists as listed)
notes: Status evidence: Searches and the Carle Illinois research facilities page show no facility with this name. Nearest matches are the Translational Oncology and Regenerative Medicine (TORM) lab announced in 2026 and the Cancer Center at Illinois Biomedical Research Center. Map entry has no link. No official page found with this exact name. Candidates: the TORM lab (announced 2026; a WCIA report says it will include the university's first cGMP clean room), the Cancer Center at Illinois Biomedical Research Center at Carle, or a Translational Research Resource Center under the Carver Biotechnology Center (seen only in a search summary, not on a fetched page). Consider dropping or relabeling once identified.

name: AxisMED
tagline: Student-run pre-incubator for medical device and health startup teams
description: A student-run pre-incubator at Carle Illinois where mixed teams of medical, engineering, and business students spend fall to spring developing a health venture through five pitch-style design reviews, workshops, and peer mentoring.
what_it_is: A student-led program at the Carle Illinois College of Medicine that forms mixed-major teams and walks them through an eight-month, Stanford Biodesign style process to build an early healthcare venture.
who_should_apply: Medical, graduate, and undergraduate students from any college who want to join or lead a healthcare venture team at the idea stage; no prior startup experience needed.
choose_this_if: You want to build a medical device or health venture with clinicians, engineers, and business students before applying to an accelerator.
good_for: Building a medical device or health venture with an interdisciplinary team
ideal_participant: Medical, graduate, and undergraduate students interested in building healthcare technology ventures
apply_steps: Join the AxisMED Discord server | Email contact@axismed.org to ask about the application process
deadline_note: The program runs on the academic year, starting in fall and ending in spring (Carle Illinois AxisMED page). A 2022 Carle Illinois news story describes recruiting each fall for the new cohort. No 2026 to 2027 recruitment dates are posted.
notes: Status evidence: The Carle Illinois AxisMED page (copyright 2026) lists a current student leadership team, including a recruitment chair, but shows no 2026 to 2027 cohort or recruitment dates. Most recent dated outcomes on the page are from 2024. Founded in 2020 to 2021 by four Carle Illinois medical students; first full cohort ran 2021 to 2022. Each team is led by a Carle Illinois medical student with members from across campus (2022 news). The AMELIA team won $10,000 at the 2024 Cozad New Venture Challenge, which is a competition prize, not an AxisMED grant. axismed.org returned no readable content.

name: CUBE Consulting
tagline: Student consulting group doing business, engineering, and design projects for clients
description: CUBE Consulting is a student-run group at UIUC where undergraduate teams do semester-long business, engineering, and design projects for real clients. Any major and year can apply, and case training is provided during recruitment.
what_it_is: A student-run consulting organization where teams of UIUC undergraduates spend one semester on a strategy, engineering, or design project for a startup, local business, or large company.
who_should_apply: Undergraduates of any major and any year, freshman through senior; no consulting experience required.
choose_this_if: You want to do hands-on client work across business, engineering, and design with a team, and you are open to case interviews.
good_for: Getting real client consulting experience across business, engineering, and design
ideal_participant: Undergraduates of any major and year who want client consulting experience
apply_steps: Submit the short online application with your resume and prompt answers | Attend the info and networking nights | Complete the invite-only case and behavioral interviews
deadline_note: Fall 2026 first-round applications closed Aug 28, 2026 at 11:59 pm, with final decisions Sep 10, 2026 (CUBE Join Us page). Recruitment runs each semester; Spring 2027 dates are not posted yet.
notes: Status evidence: The CUBE homepage says 7 teams are working with 7 clients this semester, and the Join Us page shows the Fall 2026 recruitment timeline (copyright 2026). Running since 2012 and affiliated with the Junior Enterprise network. Projects last 12 to 14 weeks with a project manager, 3 to 5 consultants, and an executive partner. Recruitment takes about two weeks from application to offer. Applicants also attend Quad Day and a case workshop during the fall cycle.

name: EntreCORPS
tagline: Free student consulting for early-stage startups, and a way to join as a consultant
description: EntreCORPS is a pro bono consulting group in Gies where student teams research markets and customers for early-stage startups each semester. Students of any major gain project and team experience, and campus startups can apply for free help.
what_it_is: A student-run, no-cost consulting group in the Gies College of Business where teams of student consultants do market and customer research for early-stage startups in the Illinois ecosystem.
who_should_apply: Students of any major and year, from freshmen to master's students, who want startup consulting experience; early-stage founders can also request free help.
choose_this_if: You want to consult for real startups as a student, or you run an early startup and need free market research.
good_for: Free startup consulting, or consulting experience for students
parent_org: Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, Gies College of Business
ideal_participant: Students of any major or year who want startup consulting experience; early-stage startups in the Illinois ecosystem that need market or customer research
apply_steps: Attend an EntreCORPS info session listed on the homepage
deadline_note: Recruits each semester. The EntreCORPS homepage lists fall info sessions on Aug 29 and Aug 30 (year not stated). Past spring cycles ran from late January to early February (Feb 1, 2025 deadline per a Gies social post). No Spring 2027 date is posted.
cost_or_funding: Free (pro bono) for client startups per giesgroups.illinois.edu/entrecorps/home/
notes: Status evidence: A Jan 14, 2026 Gies news article says up to nine EntreCORPS teams consult with startups each semester; the group site carries a 2026 copyright. Part of the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship. Teams have a project manager, a senior consultant, and four or five consultants, and work under NDAs. Site reports 90+ clients served. The old entrecorps.illinois.edu/apply page is outdated and did not load.

name: Founders: Illinois Entrepreneurs
tagline: Open-membership student entrepreneurship club for meeting cofounders and mentors
description: Founders: Illinois Entrepreneurs is a student club that helps UIUC students meet mentors, potential cofounders, and startup competitions. Membership is open to any student and is joined through the club's OneIllinois page.
what_it_is: A registered student organization founded around 2013 that promotes entrepreneurship at UIUC by connecting students with mentors, possible cofounders, and startup competitions.
who_should_apply: Any UIUC student at any stage, from curious to already building; no application is described, members join through OneIllinois.
choose_this_if: You want to meet other student founders in a low-commitment way and hear about campus startup events.
good_for: Meeting cofounders and other student entrepreneurs
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student curious about starting or growing a business
apply_steps: Open the Founders club signup page on OneIllinois and sign in | Select the group and click Join
deadline_note: No recruitment cycle or deadline is listed; the OneIllinois signup page offers a Join button and lists lifetime membership. No upcoming events were posted on the OneIllinois events page as of Oct 13, 2026.
notes: Status evidence: The OneIllinois page (copyright 2026) lists 7 officers and 17 members but shows no upcoming events. The club's own site, founders.illinois.edu, loads only over plain http (the https version fails) and its content is dated 2021. The club's own website is http://founders.illinois.edu/ (a GitHub Pages site); https fails with a certificate error, and the http version is dated 2021 and describes past programs such as the 54 startup weekend, the Forge Midwest conference, a startup career fair, and an 8-week Startup Bootcamp. OneIllinois lists an affiliation with the Grainger College of Engineering. LinkedIn gives a founding year of 2013. Do not confuse this club with Founders Week (Sep 30 to Oct 3, 2026), which is run by Entrepreneurship at Illinois.

name: Illinois Business Consulting (IBC)
tagline: Large paid student consulting firm at Gies serving companies, startups, and nonprofits
description: Illinois Business Consulting is a large student-run consulting firm in Gies where teams of students work on paid semester projects for clients from startups to large companies and nonprofits, guided by professional staff.
what_it_is: A professionally staffed, student-run consulting firm in the Gies College of Business where about 260 students work in teams on fee-based semester projects for companies ranging from startups to Fortune 100 firms and nonprofits.
who_should_apply: UIUC students who want structured consulting experience and are ready for case and behavioral interviews; the official pages do not state major or year limits.
choose_this_if: You want to join a large, established consulting organization with staff mentors and a wide range of client projects.
good_for: Getting real client consulting experience, including with startups
ideal_participant: Students who want consulting experience on real business problems
apply_steps: Submit the online application form | Complete a case interview | Complete a behavioral interview
deadline_note: Fall 2026 applications were due Aug 28 at 11:59 pm per IBC's official Linktree. The Gies-hosted apply page still shows outdated Fall 2019 deadlines. No Spring 2027 date is posted.
notes: Status evidence: IBC's official Linktree advertises a Fall 2026 application and an IBC Tech Team application; the Gies IBC page describes 260+ members and ongoing client work. Founded in 1996 by Dr. Paul Magelli per the IBC About page (U.S. News says 1995). Gies page reports 1250+ projects for 500+ clients across six practice areas, with about 800 hours of work per project. Staffed by Gies professionals alongside student leaders. Also recruits for a separate IBC Tech Team. Comparable to OTCR and CUBE.

name: Illinois Enactus
tagline: Student group that builds social impact ventures for Champaign-Urbana
description: Illinois Enactus is a student group that builds small ventures tackling social and environmental problems in Champaign-Urbana and later passes them to community partners. It recruits freshmen to juniors of any major each fall and spring.
what_it_is: A student organization in the Enactus network that starts small businesses aimed at local social and environmental problems, then hands them off to community groups to run.
who_should_apply: Freshmen, sophomores, and juniors of any major who want to work on social impact ventures; seniors are not listed as eligible.
choose_this_if: You want to build a venture that serves a social or environmental need in Champaign-Urbana with a team.
good_for: Building a social impact venture with a team
parent_org: Registered student organization, UIUC (Enactus network chapter)
ideal_participant: Freshmen, sophomores, and juniors of any major interested in social impact
apply_steps: Fill out the interest form | Submit the written application | Complete the invite-only first-round interview, social, and group case interview
deadline_note: Recruitment happens in the third week of each fall and spring semester (Enactus homepage). Fall 2026 written applications were due Sep 16, 2026 at 11:59 pm, after an info night on Sep 3 (Recruitment page). The page says to check back in Spring 2027 for the next cycle.
notes: Status evidence: Homepage says the Fall 2026 recruiting cycle has ended and lists a portfolio of 6 current projects; the Recruitment page shows the full Fall 2026 timeline. Projects have covered topics such as gender gaps for girls in STEM and language barriers for immigrants in C-U. The case interview is a team exercise where applicants design a business idea for a social issue, not a consulting case. Recruiting questions go to membership@illinoisenactus.com; company partnership questions go to operations@illinoisenactus.com. LinkedIn describes it as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

name: OTCR Consulting
tagline: Student consulting firm for business and technology strategy projects
description: OTCR Consulting is a student-run consulting firm at UIUC that handles business and technology strategy projects for clients ranging from startups to large companies. Members gain client experience and access to an alumni network.
what_it_is: A long-running student-run consulting firm that works on business strategy, technology strategy, and technology implementation projects for clients from startups to large companies.
who_should_apply: Undergraduate and graduate students, mostly from business and engineering, interested in consulting careers; official eligibility and application steps could not be verified.
choose_this_if: You want to get client consulting experience focused on technology strategy alongside business strategy.
good_for: Real client consulting experience in business and technology strategy
parent_org: Registered student organization, UIUC (Gies student groups)
ideal_participant: Undergraduates, mostly business and engineering, interested in consulting careers
deadline_note: No recruitment dates were found. The Gies group pages for OTCR returned no readable content, and searches found no 2026 recruitment posts.
notes: Status evidence: The giesgroups.illinois.edu/otcr pages load as an empty script shell; a GitHub-hosted OTCR site lists a current partner team but has no dates and is not on an official domain. Crunchbase lists the company as closed, which conflicts with LinkedIn activity. otcr.illinois.edu does not resolve, and the giesgroups.illinois.edu/otcr pages render only in a browser. A GitHub-hosted OTCR site (not on an official domain) says it was founded in 1999 and has about 60 undergraduate and graduate members; other sources say 2000. Crunchbase lists OTCR as closed, but that may be stale.

name: Product Space UIUC
tagline: Product management fellowship and client project club for students
description: Product Space UIUC runs a product management fellowship with weekly workshops, mock interviews, and a client project, then places members on semester-long product projects. It also hosts a 48-hour product hackathon. All majors are welcome.
what_it_is: A student chapter of the national Product Space network that teaches product management, product marketing, and product design in a semester fellowship, then puts members on real client product projects.
who_should_apply: Students of any major interested in product management or product design; no prior experience required.
choose_this_if: You want to learn how product managers decide what to build and get a client project for your portfolio.
good_for: Learning to build and ship products the way a startup PM does
ideal_participant: Students of any major who want product management or product design skills for a startup or tech career
apply_steps: Join the Product Space mailing list to hear when applications open | Attend a recruiting event
deadline_note: Event: Product Space Recruiting Event on Oct 28, 2026, 6:30 to 8:00 pm, listed on the chapter's OneIllinois events page. No fellowship application deadline is posted; the fellowship page says to join the mailing list to hear when applications open. A Spring 2025 fellowship had a Jan 31 deadline (LinkedIn, secondary).
notes: Status evidence: The OneIllinois events page lists a Product Space Internal Event on Oct 27, 2026 and a Recruiting Event on Oct 28, 2026; the chapter site carries a 2026 copyright. Founded August 2023. The fellowship includes weekly workshops, a client project, mock interviews, and socials. The hackathon pairs product, design, and engineering students in teams of 3 to 5 for 48 hours. No contact email is published; the site links Instagram and LinkedIn. Fall 2026 hackathon dates conflicted across sources in the earlier pass and were not rechecked here.

name: Venture Capital Association (Illini VCA)
tagline: Student club that teaches venture capital and staffs members on projects for VC firms
description: The Venture Capital Association is a UIUC student club that teaches venture investing through a semester-long analyst bootcamp, then places members on research, sourcing, and due diligence projects with partner VC firms.
what_it_is: A student organization that trains new members in how venture investors evaluate startups through a weekly analyst bootcamp, then lets interested members join an associate program doing research and due diligence for partner venture capital firms.
who_should_apply: UIUC students interested in venture capital or startup fundraising; new members start in the analyst bootcamp, and the associate program follows it.
choose_this_if: You want to learn how investors judge startups and work on real projects for venture capital firms.
good_for: Learning how investors judge startups and working on real VC projects
ideal_participant: Students interested in venture capital or in understanding how startups raise money
deadline_note: Recruits at the start of each semester. Spring 2026 analyst applications closed Feb 13, 2026 per the group's how-to-join page (search snippet, secondary). The illinivca.org application status showed applications closed on Oct 13, 2026. Spring 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Status evidence: The OneIllinois events page lists VCA Fall 2026 Analyst Bootcamp weekly meetings on Tuesdays from Oct 13 through Dec 8, 2026. Two tracks: an analyst bootcamp in the first semester, then an associate program where members work under a project manager on industry research, deal sourcing, due diligence, or portfolio consulting for a partner VC firm. The current site is illinivca.org (a script-rendered site); illinivca.com no longer resolves. Do not confuse with the Chicago-based Illinois Venture Capital Association (IVCA), a trade group whose scholar program has an Oct 29, 2026 deadline.

name: Zero2One
tagline: Student-run startup incubator with a semester cohort and pitch competition
description: Zero2One is a student-run incubator at UIUC that has guided early student startups through a 10-week cohort of workshops and mentoring, ending in its Launchpad pitch competition. Its site has not been updated since Fall 2024.
what_it_is: A student organization that has run a 10-week incubator for early student startup ideas, covering co-founder matching, customer validation, and prototyping, ending in the Launchpad pitch competition.
who_should_apply: Students of any major with an early startup idea or looking for a team; it is unclear whether a 2026 to 2027 cohort is running.
choose_this_if: You want to use a structured semester program to turn a rough idea into a pitch with peer mentors.
good_for: Developing a student startup idea in a semester cohort
ideal_participant: Students of any major with an early startup idea
deadline_note: The Zero2One website still advertises Fall 2024 incubator applications and a Nov 21 Launchpad with no year. No 2026 cohort or Launchpad dates were found on its site or OneIllinois page.
notes: Status evidence: OneIllinois lists the RSO with 3 officers and 5 members and no upcoming events; the website's newest content is the Fall 2024 incubator. One LinkedIn page is labeled no longer active. Possibly winding down or rebranded as Zero2One VC. The incubator site describes weeks 1 to 3 for ideation and co-founder matching, weeks 4 to 6 for market research and business models, weeks 7 to 8 for prototyping, and weeks 9 to 10 for the Launchpad pitch. Site claims 150+ incubator alumni and 4 cohorts. A 2024 YouTube listing cited a $1000+ Launchpad prize pool (secondary). Founded around 2020 per MechSE news.

name: AgTech Innovation Summit
tagline: Free yearly agriculture technology conference at Research Park
description: A free one-day agtech conference run by Research Park, with industry panels, a regional startup pitch competition, and networking. The 2027 summit is set for March 9, 2027 in Champaign.
what_it_is: A one-day conference in Champaign where agtech startups, investors, researchers, and companies hear panels, watch a startup pitch competition, and network.
who_should_apply: Students, researchers, and founders interested in agriculture or food technology; the page lists no eligibility limits.
choose_this_if: You want to meet agtech companies and investors in one day without paying admission.
good_for: Meeting agtech companies and investors
ideal_participant: Students, researchers, and founders working on agriculture or food technology who want industry and investor contacts
apply_steps: Join the AgTech Summit email list for updates | Register through the link on the summit page once 2027 registration opens
deadline_note: Event: summit is March 9, 2027 (save the date on the summit page). 2027 registration link not yet posted; the 2026 summit was March 10, 2026.
cost_or_funding: Free; sponsors cover the cost (per summit page)
notes: Status evidence: Summit page announces the summit returns March 9, 2027. The Research Park site also uses the shorter name 'AgTech Summit'. Search snippets say the conference is free because sponsors cover it, but the 2026 page I fetched does not state cost. The Startup World Cup Agriculture and Food Regional pitch competition was held at the 2026 summit.

name: Brand Hub Workshops and Seminars
tagline: Past branding and advertising talks from a College of Media student hub
description: Branding and advertising workshops and speaker series once run by the College of Media's Brand Hub. No events after 2023 were found and its website did not load in October 2026, so treat it as likely inactive.
what_it_is: Workshops and speaker events on branding and advertising that the College of Media's Brand Hub ran between about 2021 and 2023.
who_should_apply: Students interested in marketing or advertising, but no current events were found to join.
choose_this_if: You want to learn how brands are built from advertising professionals, and can confirm a current event first.
good_for: Learning branding from industry speakers
parent_org: Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology (Brand Hub)
ideal_participant: Students interested in branding, marketing, and advertising
deadline_note: Only 2021 to 2023 events found; no 2026 or 2027 listings.
notes: Status evidence: brandhub.illinois.edu returned nothing when fetched on 2026-10-13; search results show only 2022 era events. Brand Hub sits in the College of Media advertising department, not Gies. brandhub.illinois.edu did not load on 2026-10-13. Likely inactive; consider merging into brand-hub or removing.

name: Catalyze: Professional Networking Event
tagline: Evening tech networking and hiring mixer at EnterpriseWorks
description: A free evening mixer at EnterpriseWorks where local tech employers meet job seekers and newcomers. Research Park says it runs each fall and spring, but no 2025 or 2026 date has been posted, so it may be dormant.
what_it_is: An informal evening event where Champaign-Urbana tech companies, from startups to large firms, meet people looking for networking or full-time tech jobs.
who_should_apply: Job seekers, including graduating students, who want local tech jobs; employers and attendees register separately.
choose_this_if: You want to meet Research Park and local tech employers in a relaxed setting before graduating.
good_for: Meeting local tech employers informally
ideal_participant: Job seekers, including graduating students, looking to connect with Champaign-Urbana tech companies
apply_steps: Register as an attendee through the form on the Catalyze page
deadline_note: Research Park events page says it is held in both fall and spring. Last dated editions: Oct 26, 2021 and an undated Wednesday, Nov. 2 event (likely 2022). Not on the Research Park calendar for Oct to Dec 2026.
cost_or_funding: No fee listed; food and drink provided (per Catalyze page)
notes: Status evidence: Catalyze page shows an undated Nov. 2 event; Research Park calendar (list 5115) shows no Catalyze for Oct to Dec 2026. The event page shows no year and appears to date from about 2022. It is co-presented by Research Park, Champaign County EDC, and You're Welcome CU. The page names Carly McCroy (carly@champaigncountyedc.org) and Emily Neal (ewick@illinois.edu) as contacts, and both may be out of date. The events page still lists Catalyze without a retired notice. The event may be dormant.

name: CEO and Founders Roundtable
tagline: Invitation-only quarterly dinner for Champaign-Urbana tech CEOs
description: An invitation-only quarterly dinner where 25 to 30 Champaign-Urbana tech CEOs network and discuss operating challenges with a guest speaker. Research Park pays for it, so it is free; student founders would need an invitation.
what_it_is: A free quarterly dinner where about 25 to 30 CEOs of local high-tech companies network, hear a guest speaker, and discuss running their businesses.
who_should_apply: CEOs of Champaign-Urbana tech companies with proprietary technology; students can attend only if invited as a company CEO.

name: CU Women in Tech

name: Founders Week
tagline: Annual campus-wide week of startup talks, showcases, and networking
description: The yearly campus startup week from Entrepreneurship at Illinois, with talks, a founder showcase, and investor networking. The 2026 edition ran Sept 30 to Oct 3, 2026; 2027 dates are not posted yet.

The official page mixes a past-tense 2026 recap with an older 'sign up for Founders Week 2026' section, so parts of the page are stale. 2025 edition included a Capital Forum and Founder Showcase; about 500 attendees per a linked story. Sponsors include EnterpriseWorks, Gies, iVenture, Illinois Ventures, and Research Park.

name: Innovation Celebration
tagline: Former Champaign County awards night for local innovators, last held 2019

Recommend removing from active listings or marking discontinued.

name: Innovation Expo
tagline: Past campus fair showcasing startup support programs, last seen 2020
description: A fair co-hosted by the Landuyt Center, Innovation LLC, and the Founders student group where students met campus startup resources. The last known edition was Sept 29, 2020, so it is likely discontinued.

Possibly discontinued or replaced; no 2021 to 2026 listings found. Founders Week (Sep 30 to Oct 3, 2026) and the TE 200 Idea Fair are the closest current events. No dedicated official page exists; url is the 2020 calendar entry.

name: Innovation Living-Learning Community
tagline: Entrepreneurship-themed dorm floors with a maker workspace for first-years
description: A residence hall community in Townsend Hall for students of any major interested in startups, with a required TE 200 course, a project workspace, microgrants, and events. There is a $350 yearly program fee on top of housing.
what_it_is: A living-learning community on floors 3 to 5 of Townsend Hall where students of any major live together, take TE 200 Introduction to Innovation, and use a shared project workspace called The Garage.
who_should_apply: Incoming undergraduates of any major, mainly first-years, who want to live with other student builders.
choose_this_if: You want to live with other students starting projects and have a workspace and staff help down the hall.
good_for: Living with other student builders in your first year
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship & University Housing
ideal_participant: Undergraduates, especially first-years, of any major interested in innovation

deadline_note: Housing pages list a May 8 priority deadline for the contract and LLC essay each year, with no year stated; expect May 8, 2027 for fall 2027. New students can submit the contract 48 hours after accepting admission. Returning-resident sign-up for 2027 to 2028 begins October 19 (Housing Sign-Up page).

notes: Status evidence: Landuyt Innovation LLC page reports 2025 to 2026 highlights, including 13 microgrants; housing page is taking applications. Housing page says floors 3 to 5 of Townsend Hall; Landuyt page says Illinois Street Residence Halls (Townsend is part of ISR). First-year residents must take TE 200. Housing cost is standard University Housing rates (not stated on page).

name: Pygmalion Festival
tagline: Champaign-Urbana music and arts festival that once had a tech track
description: An annual ticketed arts and culture festival in Urbana. It used to include a tech track with a startup demo night and hackathon, but no tech programming appears for 2026, so it is of limited use for founders.

who_should_apply: Students who want a local culture festival; it no longer offers startup programming.
choose_this_if: You want a local community festival; skip it if you want startup events.

ideal_participant: Students and community members interested in C-U culture and the local tech scene

notes: Status evidence: Official site lists the September 24 to 27, 2026 festival. The festival is active, but the Pygmalion Tech Festival component (Tech Demo at Krannert, PygHack hackathon, Tech Crawl, Research Park panels) appears only in roughly 2016 to 2019 sources. The 2026 official site and coverage mention music, comedy, literature, film, and food, not tech. The tech track is likely discontinued; consider relabeling or dropping from an entrepreneurship directory.

name: Research Park Entrepreneurship Workshops
tagline: Startup skill workshops and tech meetups at Research Park and EnterpriseWorks
description: Research Park and EnterpriseWorks host startup workshops and monthly tech meetups, such as a blockchain meetup and a Data and AI user group. The workshops page is from 2019, and no formal workshops are on the calendar for fall 2026.
what_it_is: Research Park workshops on startup topics like intellectual property, pitching, customer discovery, and federal SBIR grants, plus monthly tech meetups at EnterpriseWorks.
who_should_apply: Students and early founders in Champaign-Urbana; some events, like First Friday Breakfast, are only for EnterpriseWorks startups.
choose_this_if: You want free-standing sessions on startup basics and to meet local founders and engineers.
good_for: Learning startup basics and meeting local founders
parent_org: Research Park at the University of Illinois (EnterpriseWorks)
ideal_participant: Students, researchers, and early founders in Champaign-Urbana building a startup
deadline_note: Event: Data + AI User Group meetup at EnterpriseWorks, Nov 13, 2026, noon to 1 pm. Also Champaign Blockchain Meetup Oct 16, Nov 20, and Dec 18, 2026. No workshop-style sessions listed Oct to Dec 2026.

Merged: the ecosystem map lists 'Entrepreneurship Workshops' under both EnterpriseWorks and Research Park. EnterpriseWorks is Research Park's incubator, and both point to the same single Workshops page and one shared events calendar run by Research Park, so this is treated as one series. next_deadline reflects the next calendar meetup, not a formal workshop; the First Friday Breakfasts are for EnterpriseWorks startups only.

name: Siebel Center for Design Workshops
tagline: Hands-on design thinking and maker tool workshops at Siebel Center for Design
description: Siebel Center for Design runs evening maker workshops in The Shop, such as laser cutting and sticker making, and design thinking workshops groups can request. Upcoming sessions include Oct 26 and Nov 2, 2026.
what_it_is: Short workshops at the Siebel Center for Design, including evening maker sessions on laser cutting and sticker printing, plus design thinking sessions student groups can book.
who_should_apply: Any student or student group wanting a quick, practical intro to design methods or fabrication tools; SHIFT sessions are for educators.

good_for: Short, hands-on intros to design thinking and maker tools
ideal_participant: Students or student orgs wanting a quick, practical intro to design methods or fabrication tools
apply_steps: Pick a session from the SCD workshops calendar | For a group design thinking workshop, submit a request at least three weeks ahead
deadline_note: Event: Intro to Lasers (Laser Lamps), Oct 19, 2026, 4:30 to 7:00 pm, The Shop. Then Intro to Rotary Lasers Oct 26 and Intro to Print Lab Nov 2, 2026. SHIFT Max (educators only) applications run Feb 1 to Mar 8, 2027.
notes: Status evidence: SCD workshops page lists student maker sessions on Oct 19, Oct 26, and Nov 2, 2026. Oct 15 SHIFT Spark, Oct 19 Intro to Lasers at The Shop). SHIFT Spark and SHIFT Max are aimed at educators, not students. HCD Workshops for student orgs at /outreach/HCDWorkshops.

name: Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Workshop
tagline: Selective winter break trip to meet Silicon Valley founders and investors
description: A selective January trip for about 25 on-campus UIUC students to meet Silicon Valley founders, investors, and alumni. Airfare, lodging, and most meals are arranged; a fee applies with aid available. Applications open each fall.
what_it_is: A week-long January trip where about 25 selected UIUC students visit startups, tech companies, venture capitalists, and alumni in Silicon Valley, with travel arranged by the Landuyt Center.
who_should_apply: Full-time, on-campus UIUC undergrad or grad students of any stage; online degree students are not eligible.

good_for: Seeing Silicon Valley startups and investors up close
ideal_participant: Full-time, on-campus UIUC students curious about startups and tech careers

notes: Status evidence: Program page says applications are closed for the January 2027 workshop, which means the trip is running this cycle. Online degree students are not eligible. Counts as an elective option for the Technology Commercialization certificate.

name: SocialFuse
tagline: Landuyt pitch night for finding startup teammates
description: A Landuyt Center pitch and networking night where students share ideas, find teammates, and learn about the Cozad startup competition. The fall 2026 edition is Nov 5, 2026, 5 to 7 pm at the Campus Instructional Facility; RSVP online.
what_it_is: A recurring evening event from the Landuyt Center where students pitch ideas, recruit teammates, network, and ask questions about the Cozad New Venture Challenge startup competition.
who_should_apply: Any student with an early idea or looking to join a team; no prototype needed and you can just watch.
choose_this_if: You want to find cofounders or practice a short pitch in a low-pressure room.
good_for: Finding cofounders and practicing a quick pitch
ideal_participant: Students looking for teammates or wanting to share an early idea

deadline_note: Event: SocialFuse Fall26, Nov 5, 2026, 5:00 to 7:00 pm, CIF Monumental Steps (Landuyt calendar and program page). No spring 2027 date posted yet; the spring 2026 edition was paired with Cozad Info Night on Jan 28, 2026.
notes: Status evidence: Landuyt calendar and SocialFuse page both list Nov 5, 2026. Spring edition paired with Cozad Info Night (Jan 28, 2026 in last cycle). Counts as an approved event for the Innovation certificate.

name: Designer-in-Residence Program
description: EnterpriseWorks startups can get free design guidance from industrial design professor Deana McDonagh, covering user research, empathic design, early form exploration, and design strategy for their product.
