name: Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) Program
description: Free one-on-one consulting from experienced entrepreneurs on topics like fundraising, team building, value proposition, marketing, and investor readiness, plus monthly training sessions on IP, sales, and SBIR grant writing.
good_for: Getting free advice from seasoned founders on an early-stage startup
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: UIUC students, faculty, and staff, Research Park clients, or community tech entrepreneurs with an early-stage idea or startup
deadline_note: Appointments requested by online form; no deadline.
cost_or_funding: Free consulting (per program page)
notes: Program page dated 2021, but the program is still linked from current EnterpriseWorks pages. Status left Unknown since no dated 2026 EIR activity was found.

name: Illinois FAST Center (SBIR/STTR Assistance)
description: An EnterpriseWorks-led program that helps Illinois small businesses and researchers win federal SBIR and STTR grants through free workshops, office hours, one-on-one mentoring, and proposal reviews.
good_for: Writing a competitive SBIR or STTR grant proposal
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: Founders, researchers, and inventors anywhere in Illinois preparing an SBIR or STTR proposal

name: Intellectual Property Clinic
description: A spring-semester clinic where College of Law students, supervised by a patent attorney, draft patent applications or prepare trademark filings for selected UIUC student startups. Students get legal work worth thousands of dollars for free, paying only USPTO filing fees.
good_for: Getting a patent or trademark application drafted for free
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship & College of Law
ideal_participant: Student entrepreneurs with an invention or brand to protect
deadline_note: Clinic runs in spring only. Page lists an info night on Thurs., Oct. 8 (year not stated, likely 2026 and now past); no application deadline stated.
cost_or_funding: Free legal services; students pay USPTO filing fees (per program page)
notes: Two tracks: Patent and Trademark. Launched in 2008 with Adjunct Prof. Joseph Barich. Patent track companies get preference for the trademark track.

name: Office of Technology Management (OTM)
description: The campus office that receives invention disclosures, files patents, and licenses University of Illinois technologies to companies, including startups founded on university research. Students and researchers whose idea came out of university work use it to report the innovation and work out ownership and licensing.
good_for: Disclosing and licensing a university invention
parent_org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation
ideal_participant: Faculty, staff, and students with an invention or software developed using university resources

Office is clearly operating (2025 stats), but no 2026-dated evidence was found on the homepage, so status left Unknown. Student relevance depends on whether IP arose from university resources or employment.

name: Cancer Center at Illinois (CCIL)
description: An NCI-designated cancer research center at UIUC that funds engineering and data science approaches to cancer with seed grants and training programs. It has no startup program, but it connects researchers with Carle clinicians and translational research space.

ideal_participant: Researchers and students working on cancer-related technology, diagnostics, or therapies

Grant programs (Seed, Bridge, Planning, High-Throughput Screening) are research grants that require Cancer Center membership. Student training includes a Cancer Education Undergraduate Certificate and graduate TiME Program. Publishes an 'Innovation Insider' newsletter.

name: Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology (IGB)
description: A campus genomics and life sciences institute with a bioeconomy and entrepreneurship arm, including a summer Early Innovator Program and a lecture series. Grad students and postdocs in related research can get commercialization training, mentors, and small proof-of-concept prizes.

subcategory: Research institute with bioeconomy and entrepreneurship programs
ideal_participant: Graduate students, postdocs, and faculty doing biology or genomics research with commercial potential
deadline_note: Early Innovator Program runs 10 weeks starting the week of May 19 through end of July; page gives no year or application deadline.
cost_or_funding: Early Innovator Program top pitch winners receive up to $5,000 in proof-of-concept funding (per https://www.igb.illinois.edu/bioeconomy/igb-early-innovator-program)

Bioeconomy contact listed as Tracy Parish, Director of External Relations and Strategic Partnerships (tparish@illinois.edu). Early Innovator Program is open to University of Illinois grad students and postdocs whose work relates to an IGB theme. A search snippet from entrepreneurship.illinois.edu news referenced a 2026 Early Innovator pitch contest, not directly verified.

name: Carle Illinois College of Medicine (CI MED)
description: UIUC's engineering-based medical school, whose Office of Research and Innovation runs the Health Make-A-Thon, innovation seed grants, and medical device regulatory advising. Most funding and advising is reserved for CI MED students, though some events involve interdisciplinary student teams.
good_for: Health and medical device innovation
ideal_participant: CI MED students and faculty; other students interested in health tech via Make-A-Thon teams
deadline_note: Health Innovation Research Day was held April 3, 2026.
cost_or_funding: For CI MED students: Maker Coin of $10,000 per student across four categories; Research and Innovation Pathway Grants up to $3,000 per project (per https://medicine.illinois.edu/research-and-innovation)
notes: Status evidence: Research and Innovation page announces Health Innovation Research Day on April 3, 2026; CI MED 2026 graduation news published. Health Make-A-Thon and Health Maker Lab appear as separate map entries. Regulatory and development advising contact: yschleif@illinois.edu (CI MED faculty and students).

name: Corporate Innovation Centers
description: About 30 companies, including Fortune 500 firms, run innovation centers at Research Park to work with university faculty and hire student teams on real product and research projects. For students, these centers are the main source of paid internships and full-time job offers next to campus.
good_for: Working on industry R&D teams while in school
ideal_participant: Companies looking to open a campus innovation center. Students reach these centers through internships.

This is a service for companies, which apply to become tenants. The page says more than 800 students work at Research Park year round. The figure of about 30 innovation centers comes from the student internship FAQ. Students reach these centers through the internships entry. Status evidence is park-wide activity, not a program-specific 2026 item.

description: Research Park staff introduce startups, especially EnterpriseWorks companies, to corporations with innovation centers at the park, which can lead to partners, pilot customers, or investors. No official page describes how the service works.
good_for: Startups seeking corporate partners or pilot customers
ideal_participant: Founders of startups at EnterpriseWorks or Research Park looking for corporate partners. This is not a program students apply to directly.

The URL points to the team page because it lists Bailey Conrady, Associate Director of Community and Industry Partnerships (edenbur2@illinois.edu), the closest match for this service. The description is inferred from the ecosystem map label. Consider merging this into research-park-corporate-innovation-centers.

name: Gies College of Business
description: UIUC's business college, home of the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, which runs the iVenture Accelerator, EntreCorps consulting, and a student venture fund. ideal_participant: Students of any major interested in the business side of starting a company

name: Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology (Brand Hub)

parent_org: Charles H. Sandage Department of Advertising, College of Media

Contact email from cached site info only. Former official URL https://brandhub.illinois.edu/ did not resolve (DNS failure) on 2026-10-13.

name: Illinois Social Innovation
description: A campus-wide Gies initiative that trains students to tackle social and environmental problems through social entrepreneurship coursework, global programs, and hands-on impact projects. ideal_participant: UIUC students interested in social entrepreneurship and changemaking, from any major

The School of Social Work also has an Illinois Social Innovation page.

ideal_participant: Any UIUC student exploring a startup idea or entrepreneurship coursework

name: National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA)
description: UIUC's supercomputing and data science center, which works with companies through an Industry Partner Program and runs student programs such as the SPIN undergraduate internship and the Fiddler Innovation Fellowship. Student founders can tap its computing resources, experts, and industry network.

good_for: Commercializing university research and finding campus startup support
ideal_participant: Graduate students and faculty with research they want to commercialize

description: Gies Business's entrepreneurship hub, now presented as the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship. It runs the iVenture Accelerator, the EntreCORPS student consulting group, and student investing programs, and supports the entrepreneurship minor.

ideal_participant: UIUC students building a startup or wanting hands-on venture experience

name: Champaign County Economic Development Corporation

name: Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE)
tagline: Midwest quantum science consortium with a paid summer undergrad research fellowship
description: A Midwest quantum consortium of universities, labs, and companies. Undergrads can apply for its Open Quantum Initiative fellowship, a 10 week summer research placement with a $7,000 stipend, housing, and travel, and browse quantum jobs and events.

ideal_participant: Students and founders in quantum science and engineering

UIUC is a placement site for OQI fellows and IQUIST helped fund the Summer 2024 OQI program. Q-Ready (free, for students in IL, WI, IN) seen only in search snippets, not verified on an official page. UIUC member status not clearly labeled on homepage.

name: Discovery Partners Institute (DPI)
tagline: U of I System's Chicago tech institute, home of the paid City Scholars internship
description: The U of I System's Chicago institute for AI research and industry partnerships. UIUC juniors and seniors in CS, CE, or EE can apply to City Scholars, a semester in Chicago with a part-time paid internship plus classes.

who_should_apply: UIUC undergrads with junior standing in CS, CS + X, computer engineering, or electrical engineering who have taken or are taking the required course (3.2 GPA recommended).
choose_this_if: You want to spend a semester in Chicago working at a tech company while taking UIUC classes.
good_for: Spending a semester working in Chicago tech
subcategory: University of Illinois System Chicago institute

notes: Status evidence: City Scholars application page shows a Spring 2027 cohort running January 19 to May 5, 2027; DPI homepage features a September 2026 op-ed. DPI's other talent programs target K-12 and community college students. City Scholars is run by Grainger and hosted at DPI; it may deserve its own directory entry. No email listed; contact via https://dpi.illinois.edu/about/contact.

name: Duality Quantum Accelerator
tagline: Quantum startup accelerator, now run as the quantum track of Alchemist Chicago

what_it_is: A Chicago accelerator for quantum technology startups, founded by UChicago's Polsky Center and the Chicago Quantum Exchange with UIUC as a founding partner, that now runs inside the Alchemist Chicago deep tech accelerator.
who_should_apply: Pre-seed or seed quantum startups with at least two technical co-founders who can attend in person in Chicago and San Francisco; student founders qualify only with a formed team at that stage.

good_for: Launching a quantum hardware or software startup
parent_org: Polsky Center (UChicago) and Chicago Quantum Exchange
ideal_participant: Founders of early-stage quantum technology startups

name: Engineering Innovation Leadership Council (EILC)

name: Entrepreneurial Living-Learning Community (ELLC) Roundtable
tagline: Yearly meeting of staff who run entrepreneurship dorm communities

name: IBM-Illinois Discovery Accelerator Institute
tagline: IBM and UIUC research partnership in AI systems and quantum computing

name: Illinois Innovation Network (IIN)
tagline: U of I System network of innovation hubs with a free annual conference
description: A statewide U of I System network of innovation hubs that runs seed grants and an annual conference. Students attend free, and senior undergrads and grad students can show posters. The 2026 conference is October 22 to 23 at SIUE.
what_it_is: A University of Illinois System network of research and innovation hubs across the state, including one at UIUC, that awards seed grants and holds a yearly conference with a student poster session.

name: Illinois Small Business Development Center at Champaign County EDC
tagline: Free one-on-one advising for people starting a small business in Champaign County

Search results cite a May 2026 CCEDC announcement naming Lauren Gramly as director (not fetched directly).

Most recent dated item on illinoisincubators.org is the 2024 America's Seed Fund Road Tour; no 2025 or 2026 activity found. Location is statewide Illinois (closest allowed value used).

name: Jump ARCHES (Applied Research for Community Health through Engineering and Simulation)
tagline: Health care engineering research grants with OSF clinicians, plus a summer internship
description: A Grainger Engineering and OSF HealthCare partnership that funds joint engineer and clinician health research. Grants go to faculty teams; UIUC students can join funded projects through a summer internship.

ideal_participant: Grainger faculty with an OSF clinical partner; students seeking health tech research or internships

Award amounts are in the Award Guidelines document, not checked. Symposium audience and cost not stated.

name: Kern Entrepreneurial Engineering Network (KEEN)
tagline: National network of engineering schools that teaches an entrepreneurial mindset

name: Mayo Clinic & Illinois Alliance for Technology-Based Healthcare
tagline: Mayo Clinic and UIUC partnership offering summer research and grad fellowships at Mayo
description: A Mayo Clinic and University of Illinois partnership. UIUC sophomores and juniors can apply for paid summer research at Mayo (SURF, HERE), and grad students can apply for a funded fellowship with a year at Mayo.
what_it_is: A research partnership between Mayo Clinic and the University of Illinois that sends UIUC undergrads to paid summer research programs at Mayo and funds UIUC grad students to spend at least a year doing health tech research there.
who_should_apply: UIUC sophomores and juniors with at least a 3.0 GPA aiming for research or clinical careers (summer programs), or UIUC grad students with two or more years left (fellowship).
choose_this_if: You want a funded summer or year-long research stint working with Mayo Clinic doctors and scientists in Rochester, Minnesota.

parent_org: Mayo Clinic and University of Illinois (overseen by the Interdisciplinary Health Sciences Institute)
ideal_participant: UIUC grad students in health tech research; undergrads seeking summer research at Mayo
apply_steps: Submit the Illinois SURF pre-selection form with a personal statement and transcript by Nov 1, 2026 | Have two recommenders email letters to LeaAnn Carson | If chosen, submit the Mayo Clinic SURF application by Feb 3, 2027

Fellowship contact LeaAnn Carson (lcarson@illinois.edu). HERE updates list: https://groups.webservices.illinois.edu/subscribe/139379.

name: Midwest Engineering Entrepreneurship Network (MEEN)

name: University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) Innovation and Entrepreneurship
tagline: Startup and innovation programs at the University of Illinois Chicago campus
description: The University of Illinois Chicago's innovation center, incubators, and tech transfer office. Most programs are for UIC affiliates, but a few accept outside Chicago founders, useful for UIUC founders moving to Chicago.
what_it_is: The Chicago campus of the University of Illinois System, whose Innovation Center, incubators, and tech transfer office mainly serve UIC students, faculty, and corporate partners.
who_should_apply: Mostly not open to UIUC students; a few UIC programs, such as the Entrepreneurial Support Program and the Health Technology Incubator, accept outside Chicago founders.
choose_this_if: You are a founder based in Chicago looking for incubator space or partners within the University of Illinois System.
good_for: Chicago connections within the University of Illinois System
ideal_participant: UIC affiliates; UIUC founders looking for Chicago-area partners or system-wide programs
deadline_note: No program-wide deadline; the UIC Innovation Center homepage lists no 2026 dates. The Summer Venture Accelerator did not run in summer 2025.
notes: Status evidence: innovationcenter.uic.edu lists ongoing labs, workshops, and student programs but no dated 2026 activity. UIC OTM services page shows most programs (Innovation Center incubation, MADLab, OTM, UICentre, CCTS) are UIC-only. Exceptions: the UIC Entrepreneurial Support Program (College of Business) is open to Chicagoland entrepreneurs, and the Health Technology Incubator rents space to non-UIC startups, so a UIUC founder based in Chicago could use those as a member of the public.
